# R260 — Pristine official auto and worker safety gates in the SYCL build

Date: 2026-10-12 (JST). Read-only audit of pristine U v0.1.43, requested HEAD `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`. No command from the project, compiler/build, test/import, GPU/device/process query, Git operation, cleanup, or source edit was performed. This is an eligibility/blocker report, not an execution authorization or performance result.

## Decision

The current measured official cache128/cache512 model arms are the serial verifier-window route, as supplied by Main; R247/R254 likewise distinguish `read_windows8` from batched Prefill. Keep that route as the baseline.

There is a naming distinction to preserve: R245's cache candidate is `--expert-cache auto` (cache sizing), plus `--pool-workers 3`. It does not nominate `--prefill auto`. `--prefill auto` selects the separate batched Prefill path and was excluded for the large 32K prompt in R238. Do not conflate the two “auto” controls.

- **`--prefill auto`: blocked for this B570/device property state if it routes the long prompt through batched Prefill.** The source has no host-atomic capability gate and no automatic fallback from an unsupported marker poll to `read_windows` or a step-synchronized Prefill. Bare `auto` has an 8192-token ceiling; a 32,768-token prompt has 32,767 conditioning positions and therefore multiple Prefill chunks. The PLE double-buffer sequence-marker poll is reachable after earlier chunks. A routed nonresident unpinned miss can also reach the Stager's separate `done_seq` volatile poll. With the reported host/shared-atomic capability false, those concurrent host/device host-USM marker paths are not admitted. Exact auto chunk and ring sizes depend on live memory/cache/profile values and cannot be inferred here.
- **`--pool-workers 3`: source-eligible as a separate controlled candidate on the already-admitted serial window route.** The option sets three worker threads literally; the default `host_works=true` also makes the serving/owner thread drain CPU jobs, so it can mean up to four CPU job consumers. It does not select the batched route, alter host-USM marker semantics, or invoke a GPU atomic. This source finding does not establish that three is faster or that a particular run executed the intended count/route. Require the Main-owned baseline to close first and capture startup worker/topology/host-participation plus unchanged route/cache receipts before any measurement.

No combined cache/worker or cache/adaptation screen is proposed here.

## Route and auto selection in the actual SYCL source

The target build is the U tree's SYCL CMake project. `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` resolves `src/program/generate.cpp` into the `strata` executable and `src/core/verify.cpp` into `strata_engine`; the source files are `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp` and `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`. The CPU pool implementation is the common root `src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp`, linked by the SYCL CMake target. This is the relevant SYCL build path, not an inference from only generic `src/program/generate.cpp` or `src/core/verify.cpp`.

`--prefill auto` is parsed separately from `--short-read`. Bare auto's `prefill_auto_max` defaults to 8192; an explicit `auto:N` or `STRATA_PREFILL_AUTO_MAX` can raise the cap to 16,384 or 32,768, subject to context. In the serve request loop, `windows_ok(a,b)` rejects a segment when `b-a > req_short_read` (or other window exclusions apply). A segment accepted by `windows_ok` goes through verifier `read_windows`; a rejected long segment can go through the batched prompt path. Merely adding `--prefill auto` does not convert an accepted serial `read_windows` segment into batched Prefill, nor does it prove that every segment remains accepted. The request's exact source segmentation, `short_read`, route, and logs must be retained to know which code ran.

When batched Prefill is selected, auto sizing is memory/cache planning, not a synchronization-safety predicate. `plan_lend` uses `Prefill::bytes_needed`, cache slot/byte extents, a lend percentage and the ring-budget policy to choose chunk and lend volume. Bare auto scans up to 8192 by default; ring-bytes mode tries to preserve the configured/default ring budget and chooses the largest fitting 256-token chunk. If lending cannot be used (`no_prefill_borrow`, missing profile/cache, or no lendable slots in the request path), the code turns auto off or selects a small owned-buffer chunk. These outcomes remain in batched Prefill when that path was chosen; they do not fall back to serial verifier windows. `STRATA_PREFILL_AUTO_MAX`, ring controls, available VRAM, profile/cache and request length can alter the selected chunk/ring. Only the actual startup and per-request receipts can establish the selected values.

For `n_batched=32767`, a bare-auto maximum of 8192 cannot cover the segment in one chunk. R238's concrete `--short-read 0 --prefill 8192` path was four chunks (8192 + 8192 + 8192 + 8191). If a bare-auto planner chooses a smaller chunk, it remains multi-chunk. R238 found the PLE marker poll after chunks when another chunk follows, and also the Stager marker poll on routed nonresident unpinned expert copies. The code does not query `usm_atomic_host_allocations` before enabling either path, and its fallback for an unlendable auto request only changes buffer/chunk selection. It does not route to a serialized mode that makes those polls safe.

A theoretical single-chunk long `auto:32768` changes the PLE cross-chunk reachability, but is not admitted by this report: it is outside bare-auto's cap, has a much larger allocation/lend problem, and does not establish that Stager `done_seq` is unreachable for every routed miss. It requires a separate source/runtime/route proof and exact memory/capacity receipt; no such proof is supplied here.

## Exact host-USM blocker and distinction from the admitted window route

R238 identifies the batched-Prefill completion families in U's `sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: PLE's double-buffer `ple_done_seq` and the Stager's `done_seq`. Device queue work writes markers in host-visible memory while host code polls them using volatile loads. The PLE inter-chunk wait is reachable in a multi-chunk prompt; the Stager wait is reachable for the nonresident unpinned staging branch. R238 audits that changing PLE arithmetic, first-chunk behavior, stream-all/issuer/ring settings or copy-queue choice does not, by itself, remove both marker reads. A larger ring delays reuse but is not a synchronization proof.

The supplied property state says host/shared atomic support is false. R247 is careful that device-USM support and max-allocation are separate facts; the active cache is a device allocation, while the verifier/prefill handshake storage may be host-USM. Do not turn a successful cache allocation or presence of device USM into permission for concurrent host/device marker access. The exact aspect name in the prior packet is `usm_atomic_host_allocations`; use the retained capability receipt for the selected device rather than a generic property or product label.

The current official measured serial `read_windows8` arms are a separate route. Verifier windows use `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`'s window/doorbell flow, and R247 reviewed that compiled-source path, the normal non-atomic doorbell build configuration, and its queue-boundary synchronization separately. R247 reports that the large-batched PLE/Stager polls from R238 are not reached merely by running the verifier window route. This route-specific boundary does not qualify batched Prefill. Conversely, observing more fully resident groups within a verifier window does not establish whole-stage all-residency or remove all serve boundaries.

`sycl/src/core/verify.cpp` also has `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED` as a distinct opt-in, segmented verifier mode. Its comments describe host stores raised before submitting each segment; `mapped()` uses ordinary host USM in that mode unless uncached host memory is requested. Do not silently change this flag or infer its active state from the word “windows”; the current run's environment receipt controls. The safety finding here is limited to the separate multi-chunk Prefill marker polls and the supplied false host-atomic capability.

## Worker-count gate

`sycl/src/program/generate.cpp` parses positive `--pool-workers N` directly into `o.pool_workers`; startup constructs `ExpertPool(o.pool_workers, pin=true, host_works=!o.no_host_worker, ...)`. In root `src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp`, a positive N assigns exactly N worker threads, and `run_phase` additionally calls `drain(-1,...)` from the host when `host_works_` is true. Therefore `--pool-workers 3` means three pinned workers plus the host participating by default, not three total CPU participants. The startup line reporting effective workers, core assignments and host participation is the minimum proof that the option had the intended effect. Actual CPU topology is not re-queried here.

This is a host pool adjustment and has no source predicate that enables the batched PLE/Stager polls or changes queue/device-USM behavior. It is consequently the only R245 candidate here with no newly identified host/shared-atomic blocker on the already-admitted route. It remains an experiment, not a recommended setting: record the current host core/worker topology, all candidate environment/arguments, same cache and serial window route, CPU miss jobs, prompt/decode timing separately, and ordinary correctness/fault/progress/normal-close gates. Do not infer the 5600X worker optimum from generic pool history or a source comment. The target measurement itself must remain serialized under Main's owner protocol.

## What is still required before a decision to run

- For any `--prefill auto` run, prove from the exact request route that the long part is not accepted by `read_windows`, then do not launch the batched route until a reviewed synchronization solution covers both PLE and Stager marker access, or a bounded source/route receipt proves every unsafe poll unreachable for the whole prompt. Current cache128/512, one successful allocation, a larger ring, or a smaller auto chunk does not satisfy this gate.
- A `--pool-workers 3` candidate can only follow closure of the active Main run and confirmation it is not already sampled. Preserve the same serial windows8 request, cache, binary, profile/model, source mode, and other settings. Capture the startup's actual count/pinning/host participation and actual CPU-miss work. Source inspection alone is not permission to run, and does not predict benefit.
- No gate in this audit establishes whether upstream U has been globally settings-optimized. The measured cache128/cache512 records establish those specific serial-window settings only. Other settings and the batched route remain unmeasured or excluded as stated; do not describe U as either fully optimized or merely stock from these two cache results.
